topics.label: Introduction and course overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the cancer biology lecture series, its learning objectives, and the pedagogical approach for the diverse student audience.

topics.label: Cancer as a failure of cellular differentiation and tissue architecture
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how genetic alterations disrupt normal differentiation programs and tissue organization, and address the experimental approaches used to study these cellular abnormalities.

topics.label: Distinguishing benign and malignant tumors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how benign and malignant tumors are differentiated through their invasive behavior, histological progression, and diagnostic nomenclature.

topics.label: Mechanisms of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses the mechanical and physiological processes through which primary and metastatic tumors cause illness and death in patients.

topics.label: Cancer incidence across humans and animal species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the epidemiological distribution of cancer types in humans and compare tumor incidence across diverse animal taxa.

topics.label: Principles and applications of clinical cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the clinical rationale for early cancer detection and evaluate the methods and effectiveness of population screening programs across various cancer types.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by referencing the learning outcomes and providing directions for upcoming practicals and lectures.
